title: I’m Up and Down, and Round and Round

topics.title: Definitions and symmetries of a circle

concepts.learning_objective: Define a circle as the locus of points on a plane equidistant from a given point, and identify its centre and radius.
Identify chords and diameters and recognise the diameter as the longest chord.
Describe the complete rotational symmetry of a circle and its lines of reflection symmetry.

topics.title: Circles through given points and the circumcircle

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why infinitely many circles pass through two points, with centres on the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining them.
Explain why exactly one circle passes through three non-collinear points and locate the circumcentre of a triangle.

topics.title: Chords and the angles they subtend at the centre

concepts.learning_objective: Use congruence to show that equal chords subtend equal angles at the centre, and conversely.

topics.title: Midpoints and perpendicular bisectors of chords

concepts.learning_objective: Apply the results that the line from the centre to the midpoint of a chord is perpendicular to it and the perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord.

topics.title: Distance of chords from the centre

concepts.learning_objective: Apply the results that equal chords are equidistant from the centre and equidistant chords are equal.
Compare distances of unequal chords from the centre and compute chord lengths using the Baudhayana-Pythagoras theorem.
Distinguish major and minor arcs by the angle they subtend at the centre.
Apply the theorem that the angle subtended by an arc at the centre is double the angle at any point on the circle outside the arc.
Use the corollary that a diameter subtends a right angle at any point on the circle.
Determine when four points are concyclic using equal angles subtended by a segment.
Apply the result that opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary, and its converse.
